name: Engine Cooling (high-temperature circuit)
description: Engine coolant circuit: radiator, fans/shroud, thermostat, hoses, pressurized surge/degas tank, vent lines and heater delete. The LT4 supercharger low-temperature loop is in engine-support.intercooler-loop.

components.name: Radiator (engine high-temperature circuit)
components.description: Cross-flow aluminum radiator that rejects engine heat. The ZL1 is part of an 11-heat-exchanger cooling package; for sustained road racing a thicker dual/triple-pass race radiator with a fully sealed duct is the usual upgrade.
components.location: Nose of the car behind the grille, rear-most core in the front heat-exchanger stack (behind the intercooler HX/condenser position).

factory.name: GM ZL1 aluminum/plastic-tank radiator
factory.notes: Delete A/C condenser on a race car to clear airflow (body/electrical teams coordinate).

raceOptions.name: PWR custom double-pass all-aluminum race radiator
C&R Racing custom radiator (Trans Am / IMSA style)

specs.Inlet/outlet: 1.5 in / 1.75 in hose necks or -20 AN

hardware.spec: M6 x 1.0 flange bolt into support
hardware.notes: Radiator floats on rubber isolators—do not clamp hard.

installNotes: Mount radiator on rubber isolators top and bottom; it must not touch the stack frame directly.
Seal every gap between the fascia opening and the core with foam/aluminum ducting so 100% of the inlet air goes through the core.
Fill and bleed after hoses and surge tank are installed (phase 11).
inspection: Check for leaks at tanks and necks

components.name: Radiator rubber isolators / mounting pins
components.description: Rubber grommets/cushions the radiator pins sit in, top and bottom. Prevent vibration cracking of tank seams.
components.location: Upper and lower radiator support, both sides.
installNotes: Replace if hardened or cracked at every rebuild.

modelRef.dimensions: ~30 mm OD x 25 mm rubber grommets on 10-12 mm radiator pins
modelRef.features: Black rubber stepped grommet; one each top/bottom corner

components.name: Electric cooling fan(s)
components.description: Electric pusher/puller fans for low-speed and pit-lane cooling. At racing speed the ram air does the work; fans should be PWM-controlled by the ECU/PDM and the shroud should have flap valves or open area so it does not block high-speed airflow.
components.location: Behind the radiator, mounted to the shroud.

factory.name: GM ZL1 brushless electric cooling fan (in shroud)
factory.notes: Fan quantity/size differs by trim; verify on your car.

installNotes: Fuse/feeder per PDM channel rating; use a dedicated relay or PDM channel per fan.
inspection: Run fan test at each event, check blades for debris strike

components.name: Fan shroud
components.description: Sheet aluminum or composite shroud that ducts fan suction across the whole core; race shrouds include rubber flap doors that open at speed.
components.location: Back face of the radiator.
installNotes: Keep >= 25 mm between fan blades and engine/water pump pulley.
inspection: Check for cracks at mounting tabs

modelRef.features: Black plastic full shroud, round venturi opening for single fan, rubber flapper doors, clips to radiator tank tops

components.name: Fan control (ECU/PDM output + optional standalone controller)
components.description: Commands fan speed from coolant temperature. On a race car this is usually a PWM PDM channel (e.g., MoTeC PDM / ECUMaster PMU) commanded by the ECU, with a manual override switch on the dash.
components.location: Logic in PDM; optional controller module on the radiator support.

hardware.spec: M5/M6

installNotes: Electrical team owns wiring; this entry documents the cooling logic.
inspection: Verify fan-on temperature in data each event

images.title: Dorman 621-984 engine cooling fan assembly (Camaro 2017-20, brushless, plastic shroud)

modelRef.features: Black finned module with connector, on the shroud back (or PDM output)

components.name: Upper radiator hose (engine outlet to radiator inlet)
components.description: Hot coolant from the engine water outlet to the radiator inlet tank. Race builds use 4-ply silicone or aluminum hard pipe with short silicone couplers (or -20 AN).
components.location: Front top of engine to upper radiator tank.

factory.name: GM ZL1 molded rubber upper hose with quick-connect

raceOptions.name: 1.5 in aluminum hard pipe + silicone joiners

hardware.spec: Stainless T-bolt clamp sized for 1.5 in hose OD
hardware.notes: Snug until silicone just bulges; re-torque after first heat cycle. OEM spring clamps are also acceptable on rubber hose.

installNotes: Avoid sharp bends; support long hard-pipe runs with cushioned clamps.
inspection: Squeeze test for softness; check clamps after heat cycle

modelRef.features: Black molded EPDM hose, GM quick-connect at engine outlet, spring clamp at radiator neck

components.name: Lower radiator hose (radiator outlet to water pump inlet/thermostat)
components.description: Cooled coolant from the radiator outlet tank to the thermostat housing on the water pump inlet. Must resist collapse under pump suction—use a hose with an internal spring or hard pipe.
components.location: Lower right of radiator to front lower of engine.

factory.name: GM ZL1 lower hose with quick-connect

hardware.spec: Stainless T-bolt clamp sized for 1.75 in hose OD
hardware.notes: Snug until silicone just bulges; re-torque after first heat cycle. OEM spring clamps are also acceptable on rubber hose.

installNotes: Keep away from dry-sump belt and headers; heat sleeve if within 75 mm of exhaust.
inspection: Check for collapse at high rpm (look for overheating at speed)

modelRef.features: Black molded hose, quick-connect at thermostat housing

components.name: Water pump gasket / seals (pump owned by engine team)
components.description: The Gen V LT mechanical water pump bolts to the front of the block and is driven by the accessory belt (engine system). This entry covers the coolant-side interface: pump-to-block gasket/O-rings and the hose connections the cooling team plumbs to.
components.location: Front of engine, centered.

factory.name: GM Gen V LT water pump with housing (Camaro/CTS-V pattern)
factory.notes: Camaro/CTS-V pump differs from Corvette and truck pumps (spacer kits exist to adapt).

raceOptions.name: Electric water pump conversion (e.g., Davies Craig/Meziere) with pump delete
raceOptions.notes: Only if engine builder approves; GM pump is generally adequate at race rpm.

hardware.spec: M8 x 1.25 flange bolt (count approx.)
hardware.notes: Michigan Motorsports lists water pump-to-block 18 ft-lb; Summit lists "water pump bolts" 89 in-lb (likely housing/cover screws). Confirm with GM SI for your pump.

hardware.spec: M6 screws

installNotes: Use new gaskets/O-rings, clean sealing faces, no RTV unless specified.

images.title: Summit: Gen V LT cooling system notes

modelRef.dimensions: ~130 mm gasket/O-ring ring at pump housing
modelRef.features: Rubber O-ring seals between pump and front cover

components.name: Engine thermostat
components.description: Controls flow through the radiator. Vendors state the stock Gen V LT1/LT4 unit is rated 212 °F (100 °C); race engines commonly use a 160-180 °F unit to keep the engine cooler and give more knock margin with the supercharger.
components.location: In the thermostat housing on the water pump inlet (lower hose side).

raceOptions.name: Lingenfelter Gen V DI V8/V6 160 °F thermostat with housing
raceOptions.notes: Direct fit, listed for Camaro ZL1 2017-18.

raceOptions.name: Restrictor plate (no thermostat)
raceOptions.notes: Not recommended—use a low-temp stat for controlled warm-up.

installNotes: Install with seal/O-ring supplied; ECU tune must reflect lower operating temp (fan, fueling, DTC thresholds).
inspection: Data-log coolant temp warm-up curve each event

components.name: Thermostat housing / water inlet
components.description: Inlet neck on the water pump that holds the thermostat and receives the lower hose (and the surge-tank make-up line).
components.location: Lower front of engine on the water pump.

factory.name: GM Gen V LT water inlet/thermostat housing

hardware.spec: M6 x 1.0 flange bolt
hardware.notes: Summit lists water outlet bolts 89 in-lb; housing value assumed same—verify (MM lists 11 lb-ft for thermostat housing in an LS-era section).

installNotes: Torque evenly in two passes to avoid cracking the housing flange.

factory.name: GM Gen V LT water outlet

hardware.spec: M6 x 1.0 flange bolt
hardware.notes: Gen V value from published spec compilation (Summit Racing / Michigan Motorsports); confirm against GM service information.

components.name: Coolant surge / expansion (swirl) tank
components.description: Pressurized degas tank that is the highest point of the system. Receives air-laden coolant from the radiator vent and engine steam line, separates the air, and feeds solid coolant back to the pump inlet via the make-up line. Race builds use a fabricated aluminum swirl-pot style tank.
components.location: Passenger side of the engine bay, forward of the right strut tower and above the engine (must be the highest point of the coolant circuit).

factory.name: GM Gen 6 Camaro coolant surge tank (plastic)
factory.notes: Factory cap rated ~20 psi (aftermarket listing for 2016-2020 Camaro).

raceOptions.name: Fabricated aluminum expansion tank, 1.5-2 qt with -10 AN inlets and 3/4 in outlet

specs.Ports: 2 x -6/-8 AN vent inlets, 1 x -12/3/4 in outlet

hardware.spec: M6 into rivnuts with rubber isolators
-6 AN 37° flare (JIC-compatible), aluminum or stainless hose end
hardware.threadlocker: none — light oil on threads and 37° seat (no sealant on flares)
hardware.reuse: Inspect (replace if seat galled or cracked)
hardware.notes: Assemble flare joints at the low end of the range; aluminum fittings gall easily. If it weeps, tighten in small increments without exceeding max. Mark with torque stripe.

hardware.spec: -12 ORB (SAE J1926 straight-thread O-ring boss) port fitting with Viton/FKM O-ring
hardware.threadlocker: none — lubricate O-ring with clean oil/fuel; no thread sealant
hardware.notes: ORB seals on the O-ring, not the threads. Values are typical aluminum-port guidance; follow fitting maker (Earl's/XRP/Fragola) if listed.

installNotes: Mount above the radiator cap/highest engine point.
Fill to the cold line only—leave expansion space.
inspection: Check cold level before each session

components.name: Heater core delete / bypass loop
components.description: The heater core is deleted on a race car (or retained for windshield defog where rules require). The two heater ports are joined with a short loop so the engine still has its designed bypass flow during warm-up, or capped if the engine builder approves.
components.location: Rear of engine near the firewall.

factory.name: GM heater hoses to HVAC module (removed)

raceOptions.name: 5/8-3/4 in hose loop or AN loop

hardware.spec: Stainless T-bolt clamp sized for 5/8 in hose OD
hardware.notes: Snug until silicone just bulges; re-torque after first heat cycle. OEM spring clamps are also acceptable on rubber hose.

installNotes: Some rules require defrost—check class rules before deleting HVAC.
Cap the firewall holes with riveted aluminum blanks (fire-wall integrity).

components.name: Coolant temperature & pressure sensors (data/ECU)
components.description: ECU coolant temp sensor (factory) plus race data coolant temperature and pressure sensors. Coolant pressure logging is the earliest warning of a head gasket failure.
components.location: Water outlet / engine coolant passages.

raceOptions.name: 0-50 psi sealed sensor + NTC temp sensor (1/8 NPT)

installNotes: Place pressure sensor where it is not in an air pocket.
inspection: Compare logged pressure to cap rating

components.name: Radiator / heat-exchanger inlet ducting and seals
components.description: Sealed ducting from the grille/splitter opening to the face of the stack, with foam seals around the cores so no air bypasses. Exit air ideally vented through the hood (aero team) to reduce front lift and underhood pressure.
components.location: Between front fascia openings and the heat-exchanger stack.

raceOptions.name: 0.040 in aluminum duct with closed-cell foam seals

hardware.spec: 1/8 in or 5/32 in aluminum pop rivets / M5 rivnuts

installNotes: Build duct after final radiator and splitter positions are fixed.
inspection: Check foam seals are intact and debris screen clear

components.name: Engine coolant (fill)
components.description: Factory fill is DEX-COOL 50/50. Most road-race sanctioning bodies/tracks prohibit glycol antifreeze on track (slippery spill); use distilled water with a surfactant/corrosion inhibitor (e.g., Red Line WaterWetter) unless rules allow otherwise.
components.location: Radiator, engine, surge tank.

factory.name: ACDelco DEX-COOL 50/50
factory.notes: LT4 engine cooling capacity ~11 qt (10.4 L) per forum/AMSOIL compilations—verify with owner manual.

fluids.name: Engine coolant
fluids.spec: DEX-COOL 50/50 (street) or distilled water + surfactant (track, per rules)
fluids.capacity: ~11 qt factory; race radiator may differ

installNotes: Vacuum-fill (Airlift-style) to eliminate air, then run with cap off/surge tank open until thermostat opens.
inspection: Check level cold every session; replace water/WaterWetter each season
